title: Cross-Domain Impact Analysis — Job → Network → GPU

options.content:
Cross-Domain Impact Analysis — Job → Network → GPU (DGX SuperPOD, fleet-scale)
Drill down from fleet counters to the actual affected nodes / GPUs. Every summary tile has a companion table listing the real offenders. Empty table = healthy. Use the Node filter to scope. XID / NVLink events come from logs (bottom).
● Healthy● Warning● Critical / capacity loss

panels.title: GPUs w/ HW Errors
panels.description: GPUs with ECC double-bit, uncorrectable remapped rows, or row-remap failure = capacity loss.

panels.title: GPUs Throttling
panels.description: Count of GPUs with a GENUINE FAULT throttle bit active (mask 232 = HW Slowdown, SW Thermal, HW Thermal Slowdown, HW Power Brake). Excludes GPU-idle, SW Power Cap and Sync Boost — those are normal power-limited operation at default TDP, not faults.
Busiest / most pressured nodes (root cause of NCCL storms & job stalls). Sorted by 5m load. Empty rows only shown if pressured.
panels.title: Node Resource Pressure — top loaded nodes (CPU / mem / OOM)
Layer 2 — Network Impact (NCCL socket storm / congestion)
TCP Established — top 20 nodes (NCCL socket storm)
panels.description: Top 20 nodes by established TCP connections. A sudden spike across many nodes = NCCL socket storm at job launch.

panels.title: NIC Throughput — top 20 nodes (RX+TX)
panels.description: Top 20 nodes by NIC throughput. Saturation during bad jobs starves other traffic.
Current network offenders. High established/socket counts = NCCL socket storm; RX drops = congestion / overrun. Sorted by TCP established.
panels.title: Network Offenders — TCP sockets & drops by node
Layer 3 — GPU Impact (thermals, throttling, HW errors)
GPU Temp — top 15 hottest GPUs
panels.description: Only the 15 hottest GPUs (of ~2300). Watch for outliers that drive thermal throttling.

panels.title: GPU Power — top 15 by draw
panels.description: 15 highest-power GPUs. Correlate spikes with power-brake throttling.
GPUs above 80C right now, hottest first. Empty = all cool.
panels.title: Hot GPU Outliers (> 80C)

panels.description: GPU memory (HBM) above 90C right now. Empty = healthy.
panels.title: Hot GPU Memory Outliers (> 90C)

panels.description: GPUs with ANY hardware error right now (ECC double-bit, remapped rows, row-remap failure, PCIe replays). These reduce usable cluster capacity. Empty = healthy.
panels.title: GPU Hardware-Error Offenders (capacity loss)

panels.description: DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS bitmask decoded to words, per GPU, REAL throttling only (idle/app-clock excluded). ACTIVE = that reason is currently clamping clocks. Empty = no throttling.

targets.expr: (bitmap_and(DCGM_FI_DEV_CLOCK_THROTTLE_REASONS{cluster=~"$cluster",node=~"$node"},4)) and on(node, gpu) (rate(DCGM_FI_DEV_POWER_VIOLATION{cluster=~"$cluster",node=~"$node"}[5m]) > 0) and on(node, gpu) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL{cluster=~"$cluster",node=~"$node"} > 50)

panels.title: GPU Throttle Reasons Decoded (active only)
Layer 4 — Storage Impact (slow disk / RAID → job stall)
Disk I/O Wait — top 15 nodes
panels.description: 15 nodes with highest iowait. High iowait stalls data loading and starves GPUs.

panels.title: Disk Throughput — top 15 nodes (read+write)
panels.description: Busiest disks. A collapse to near-zero under high iowait often signals degraded RAID.
Nodes with IOWait > 10% right now, worst first. Empty = storage healthy.
panels.title: Storage Offenders — high-IOWait nodes
Layer 5 — Correlated Evidence: XID / NVLink / Slurm events (logs)

panels.description: XID / NVLink error EVENTS from logs, aggregated to a count per node over the dashboard range (no DCGM XID metric exists). Highest first. Drill into the raw lines below.
panels.title: XID / NVLink Events by Node (logs)
XID / NVLink error log lines
panels.description: Raw XID / NVLink / NVRM kernel log lines. This is the source of truth for GPU fatal events.

panels.title: Kernel / GPU errors (OOM, throttle, ECC)
panels.description: Kernel errors correlated in time with the impact above.

panels.title: Slurm job events
panels.description: Slurm start/stop/failure events — tie impact back to the offending job.
